problem: Existing audio-based robot navigation assumes open space with no sound reflection, so sound sources whose direct path is occluded (only reflections reach the robot) cannot be localized, and visual odometry drifts.
motivation: Vision-only SLAM navigation fails with occluded goals or goals out of frame; audio can fill this gap, but reverberant indoor environments corrupt sound source localization. Handling reflections with a map lets the robot set a goal at the actual sound source rather than at a reflection.
key_idea: Use visual SLAM's map to perform reflection-robust sound source localization (reasoning about reflected paths) so that the navigation goal is set at the true source location.
insight: Integrating SLAM with visual odometry corrects drift, reducing average map error by about 50 pts and improving direct-path SSL accuracy by about 8 pts (abstract-level claims). The map provides the geometry needed to disambiguate reflected from direct sound paths, which is what makes the system robust in strongly reverberant conditions.
method: Visual odometry + SLAM: builds a map and corrects VO drift via SLAM integration
Sound source localization (SSL): microphone-array based direction estimation of sound sources
Reflection-robust SSL: uses the visual SLAM map to handle sources whose direct path is unavailable and localize the actual source
Goal setting and navigation: sets the goal at the estimated true source location and navigates online (audio-visual navigation)

setting.backbone: Classical pipeline: visual odometry/SLAM + microphone-array sound source localization (not learned)
setting.action_space: Navigation to a goal on the SLAM map (mobile robot motion commands)

numbers_note: abstract only; only qualitative gains (~50 pts map error improvement, ~8 pts SSL accuracy improvement) stated, no benchmark table
results: The proposed system outperforms conventional methods especially in extremely reverberant situations. SLAM+VO improved average map error by approx. 50 pts and direct-path SSL accuracy by approx. 8 pts, and online audio-visual navigation to real sound sources succeeded.
limitations: Evaluated on a specific real robot setup, not standard benchmarks
Depends on the accuracy of visual SLAM and a static environment map
compares_to: Conventional audio-based SSL/navigation methods assuming open space
